correctness.rationale: For A,B containing zero and meeting every [n,n+G], both finite-degree directed incidence graphs E_+={(i,j):i in A,j in B,0<=j-i<=G} and E_-={(i,j):0<=i-j<=G} cover each A and B vertex: at small indices zero supplies a preceding level, and at large indices the G-syndetic property does. At each occupied level the infinite-dimensional ℓ² summand partitions into finitely many infinite-dimensional edge summands. Matching the same edge summands with r^{(j-i)/2} (forward) and r^{(i-j)/2} (reverse) times unitaries gives ONTO bounded invertible direct sums, since r^{G/2}<=scalars<=1. The two identities are r^i r^{j-i}=r^j and r^j r^{i-j}=r^i. The (0,0) edge makes both operator norms exactly one, whence the nonnegative log comparison distance is attained at zero. Each A_eta contains all evens and has different precise eigenvalue support when eta differs; this gives continuum many unitarily inequivalent positive injective noncompact operators with nonclosed ranges. Taking frame vectors r^{i/2}e_{i,m} yields Bessel, not Hilbert frames. Independent exact rational enumeration checked edge cover, multipliers and identities over 256 two-pattern pairs of finite prefixes; infinite-dimensional surjectivity rests on the analytical block-partition construction, not on that finite test.
